records.title: Scaling Vision Transformers to 22 Billion Parameters
records.reason: The primary abstract and reviewed sections focus on scaling and training a vision encoder, not LLM inference/serving or inference-time compression/efficiency. Its hardware and parallelization work supports large-scale training of ViT-22B; evaluation is on vision transfer tasks, so this is outside the stated scope.
records.body_check: Primary arXiv abstract and selected HTML sections reviewed (introduction, architecture, training infrastructure/efficiency, experiments overview, conclusion, and model card). The method is a 22B-parameter vision encoder with parallel attention/MLP layers, QK normalization, parameter sharding, and asynchronous parallel linear operations to improve training stability and accelerator utilization. Evaluation covers image classification, zero-shot image classification, out-of-distribution vision, dense prediction, video classification, and related vision-model properties, not LLM inference or serving. The model card says the model is designed for research and has not been tested outside research settings. These passages describe vision training/scaling and transfer evaluation; no inference serving or inference-time efficiency result is claimed.

records.title: Explainability for Large Language Models: A Survey
records.reason: The primary abstract surveys local and global explainability methods for LLMs, organized by fine-tuning and prompting paradigms, and discusses explanation metrics and challenges. It is interpretability research, not an LLM inference/serving system or an inference-time compression/efficiency technique.
records.body_check: Primary arXiv abstract checked. It describes a taxonomy of explanation techniques for Transformer-based language models, covering local explanations of individual predictions, global explanations of model knowledge, and metrics for evaluating generated explanations. The abstract does not claim an inference or serving optimization or reduced inference cost; explanation evaluation is not an inference-efficiency evaluation. This is a clear scope mismatch, so full text was not needed.

records.title: K-BERT: Enabling Language Representation with Knowledge Graph
records.reason: The primary abstract proposes injecting knowledge-graph triples into BERT inputs using soft positions and a visible matrix to improve domain-specific language representation, reporting results on NLP tasks. It does not study generative LLM inference/serving or an inference-time efficiency technique; the stated contribution is knowledge-enhanced representation quality.
records.body_check: Primary arXiv abstract checked. K-BERT adds knowledge-graph triples to input sentences and uses soft-position embeddings and a visible matrix to limit knowledge-noise effects; it loads parameters from pretrained BERT and reports results on twelve NLP tasks, with gains on domain-specific finance, law, and medicine tasks. The abstract describes representation quality and knowledge injection, not serving, latency, throughput, or inference-time compression/efficiency. The scope mismatch is clear at abstract level; full text was not needed.
